The presence is WAITED FOR, twice.
Two spin loops, and no counted delay between them:
the pulse's length is the sensor's to choose
(60-240 us) and the host cannot know it. If no
sensor is there the first loop simply never exits,
which is the correct behaviour for a bus with no
timeout in this ISA - and the testbench
by whether the program got past this point.
Why 0xCC and not a 64-bit ROM code.
A ROM match is the addressable case: the host sends
all eight ROM bytes, the sensor compares them with its
own, and only the addressed one answers. With one
sensor on the bus that is 64 slots to learn nothing,
and it is the case that costs 64 slots of simulation.
SKIP ROM is 8 slots and is exactly right here. What
it costs is stated rather than glossed: with it, a bus
with two sensors would have BOTH answer, and the two
read streams would collide. The act claims the
Why the two halves of the exchange need different sample idioms.
A write slot: the HOST pulls the line low. A 1 is a
short low then a release; a 0 is the low held for the
A read slot: the SENSOR holds the line. A 0 leaves it
released for the rest of the slot; a 1 pulls it low
again for 1-15 us after the initiation pulse.
So in the read direction a ONE is LOW and in the
write direction a ZERO is LOW. The read path first
borrowed the write path's test and both bytes came
0xfe. A sensor that transmits its data inverted still

, which is the opposite of the DHT11 and of the
WS2812. The write path needs no shift at all - it masks the byte's own bit 0,
sends, and rotates the byte right so the next bit 0 is the next bit of the
frame. The read path shifts the accumulator
the top, so the first bit read slides down to bit 0 by the eighth.
